transcript.text: Bosch KGN34NL3AG - some days it's fine, other days it just clicks every few minutes at the back and doesn't seem to run, and the freezer starts getting soft. Then it starts working again by itself. What's going on?

That clicking sound followed by silence usually means the compressor is trying to start but tripping its thermal protection before it can get going. The most common cause of this intermittent 'click-hum-click' cycle is a failing start relay or overload device on the back of the unit; less commonly, it could be due to dust buildup causing overheating. Before we look at parts, please check two things:
1. Is there space around the fridge (at least 5cm) and are the coils at the back or underneath free from heavy dust?
2. When it clicks and stops, does the freezer get noticeably warm within a few hours, or does it stay frozen solid for longer periods? If the coils are clean and spaced well, we likely need to replace the start relay/overload kit.

The back is a bit dusty, but there is a gap behind the fridge. On a bad day the freezer warms up noticeably: the fridge reads 9C and the freezer -8C. The compressor is also very hot to touch when it is clicking.

This small component sits on the back of the fridge where the compressor is; its job is to give the compressor the extra boost it needs to start. This is a common failure on Bosch fridges and is usually fixed by replacing just the relay/overload kit rather than the whole compressor. Because this involves accessing the electrical connections on the back of the unit, I recommend having an engineer replace it for you to ensure the correct part is fitted safely. If you are handy with tools and comfortable working on the rear of a heavy appliance (switched off and unplugged), you can source a kit compatible with your model number KGN34NL3AG, but otherwise, a call-out is the safest route.
